chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' when he is an old aged man, or a woman who fears menstruation, who hastens the circumambulation of Hajj before going to Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The one who is like this, he hastens.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about the man who enters into Ihram for Hajj from Mecca, then sees the House (Kaaba) as being vacant, so he performs circumambulation by it before he goes out upon anything (to Mina). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

I said, 'The one performing Qiran or Tamattu' (literally: the one who is free/independent), when he has circumambulated the House and (performed sa'i between) Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, hastens the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, the circumambulation of the women is (to be done) after going to Mina.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: The one performing Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُفْرِدُ بِالْحَجِّ: The one performing Mufrid Hajj (Hajj alone without Umrah)
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: The circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa')

ai.seo_question: When should the circumambulation of the Kaaba be performed relative to going to Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in Hajj rituals, specifically allowing the Mufrid, Qarin, or Mutamatti' to perform Tawaf al-Hajj early if they have valid excuses like old age or fear of menstruation, as confirmed by Imam al-Rida (AS). It distinguishes this exception from the general rule where Tawaf al-Nisa' is performed after returning from Mina, highlighting the Shia juristic principle of easing burdens for those with specific needs. The narration underscores the practical application of ease (rukhas) within the structured framework of Hajj rites.
